hero.lead: A nation of 18.9 million at Africa’s western edge, now negotiating a $2.2 billion IMF programme while the World Bank builds its roads, clinics and buses.

capital.heading: Senegal is resetting its finances in the open. Next, safe water in every home.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility (staff-level agreement)
register.detail: Agreed 1 September 2026 · 36 months, subject to Board approval
register.note: Requires corrective action on past misreporting and financing assurances
register.text: Commits Senegal to a revenue strategy, stronger debt management and oversight of state enterprises.

register.name: Health system and financial protection
register.note: Health care and protection for vulnerable families
register.text: Strengthens the health system and protects the poorest households from the cost of care.

register.name: Road connectivity in the north and centre
register.text: Connects farming areas to markets and services.

register.name: Urban mobility in Dakar and secondary cities
register.text: Moves more people faster and more cheaply through Senegal’s cities.

register.name: Territorial development in Casamance and Kedougou
register.note: Services and jobs in lagging regions
register.text: Brings services and income to two regions that have waited longest.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 56 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A colourful street in Dakar, Senegal

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Groundnut and millet fields in the Senegalese countryside under a wide sky

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Baobab trees and dry savanna woodland in Senegal

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Enough to supply every home, once it is stored, treated and piped.
items.alt: The Senegal River at Saint-Louis with painted pirogues

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2021
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: Wind turbines of the Taiba Ndiaye wind farm in Senegal

items.name: The enterprises building Perfect Senegal
items.text: The Stewards are verifying the companies and social enterprises already delivering the seven basic living standards in Senegal. Suggest one to include.

coverage.gap_text: Senegalese without safely managed drinking water at home: 73 in every hundred.

guarantees.name: Food

guarantees.name: Energy
